summary: Added SIGTERM_GRACE_MS = 3000 and DEFAULT_LOG_DEPTH = 20 named constants in a new Tunable constants block at module scope.
Replaced hardcoded 3000 in killProcess() setTimeout with SIGTERM_GRACE_MS.
Updated findRecentPlanDirs() to accept a depth parameter; replaced .slice(-20) with .slice(-depth).
Updated cleanupStaleLocks() to accept depth and pass it to findRecentPlanDirs(depth).
Extended parseArgs() to detect --depth N: validates the value is a positive integer, errors with clear message and exit 1 for invalid inputs, defaults to DEFAULT_LOG_DEPTH.
Updated main() to pass opts.depth to cleanupStaleLocks(opts.depth).
Updated HELP constant and file header docstring to document --depth N.

comments.note: The HELP constant has a trailing double-newline at the end which causes it to print a blank line between the content and the shell prompt. This is intentional style (creates breathing room) but worth noting as a pattern to preserve if HELP is expanded.
No other code smells in touched areas. The depth threading (parseArgs → cleanupStaleLocks → findRecentPlanDirs) is clean and minimal.

summary: All 7 ACs met. AC1: SIGTERM_GRACE_MS=3000 (line 40) and DEFAULT_LOG_DEPTH=20 (line 41) are named module-scope constants with descriptive comments.
AC2: No magic numbers in function bodies. killProcess() uses SIGTERM_GRACE_MS in setTimeout (line 200). findRecentPlanDirs() uses .slice(-depth) not .slice(-20) (line 228).
AC3: --depth 5 accepted by parseArgs, flows to cleanupStaleLocks(5) → findRecentPlanDirs(5) → .slice(-5). Runtime: node scripts/kill-orchestrator.js --depth 5 --json exits 0.
AC4: Default parseArgs() returns depth=DEFAULT_LOG_DEPTH (20). node scripts/kill-orchestrator.js --json exits 0 confirming default-depth code path works.
AC5: Three invalid --depth cases tested: --depth 0 (‘got "0"’ error, exit 1), --depth abc (‘got "abc"’ error, exit 1), --depth with no value (‘got nothing’ error, exit 1). All pass.
AC6: No ESM import statements. Only stdlib require() calls (fs, path, readline, child_process). 'use strict' mode enforced.
AC7: 1738/1738 MCP server tests pass, 29/29 persona-helpers tests pass (confirmed from WP-001 run in same session).

comments.note: The depth threading is clean and complete: parseArgs() defaults to DEFAULT_LOG_DEPTH=20 and parses --depth N; opts.depth flows through main() into cleanupStaleLocks(opts.depth) into findRecentPlanDirs(depth) which uses .slice(-depth). No leakage of magic numbers anywhere in the call chain.

Three invalid input classes all handled correctly: --depth 0 (positive integer check), --depth abc (NaN check), --depth with no following value (undefined check). All produce descriptive 'Error: --depth requires a positive integer (got X)' messages with exit 1.

No code smells. Zero external dependencies confirmed (only stdlib: fs, path, readline, child_process). -- helpHidden/hidden flag distinction from WP-001 was already in effect before this WP, so kill-orchestrator appears in the interactive menu (key:k) but not in printHelp() output.
